advances: Ordinary planar density and its angular area transport. It tests full-centroid transfer under fixed-origin radialization.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
On a ray with unit direction $u$ let $R$ be its endpoint parameter in $D_q$. The radial integral is $R^2(1+2u_x R/3)$. With $s(x)=\sqrt{1+2x/3}$, the radial parameter map is $r\mapsto r s(ru_x)$ and has derivative $(1+ru_x)/s(ru_x)>0$ in the interior of the ray segment. The endpoint image therefore equals the prescribed radius. The map is continuous up to the endpoints and is a bijection on the interiors. Its Jacobian is $s(x)(s(x)+xs'(x))=1+x$. Both boundaries have area zero, so change of variables gives the pushforward. Each ray stays on its original side of every origin line, which proves the halfplane assertion, including for closed halfplanes.

For convexity, $X=xs(x)$ increases from $-1/\sqrt3$ to $1/\sqrt3$. Write $S(X)=s(x(X))$. In the interior $S'(X)=1/[3(1+x(X))]$, which decreases. Continuity extends concavity to both endpoints. The image has upper graph $qS(X)$ and lower graph $-S(X)$, so it is convex.

The marginal $x$-mass is $Z=\int_{-1}^{1/2}(1+x)\,dx=9/8$, and $\int_{-1}^{1/2}x(1+x)\,dx=0$. The uniform independent $y$ coordinate has mean $(q-1)/2$. In the two transformed moments, substitute $u=1+2x/3$. The antiderivative for $Z^{-1}\int x(1+x)s(x)\,dx$ is $6u^{7/2}/7-8u^{5/2}/5+2u^{3/2}/3$. The one for $\int(1+x)s(x)\,dx$ is $(3/4)(6u^{5/2}/5-2u^{3/2}/3)$. Evaluating on $[1/3,4/3]$ and dividing the second by $Z$ gives $8/(105\sqrt3)$ and $232/(135\sqrt3)$. These are respectively the transformed $x$-mean and the factor multiplying the original $y$-mean.

For $q=1$ the horizontal density section has zero first moment by the same integral and the vertical section is uniform on $[-1,1]$. Their chord endpoints are $\pm(1/\sqrt3,0)$ and $\pm(0,1)$. The displayed means give the asserted nonvanishing mismatch. For $q=2$ the two projections in direction $(-12,1)$ are $1/2$ and $-52/(945\sqrt3)$.

statement:
For $q>0$ put $D_q=[-1,1/2]\times[-1,q]$ and $f_q(x,y)=(1+x)\mathbf1_{D_q}(x,y)$. Its planar Ball radial body $B_q$, defined by $\rho_q(u)^2=2\int_0^\infty r f_q(ru)\,dr$ for unit $u$, is convex. The ray-preserving map $T(x,y)=\sqrt{1+2x/3}(x,y)$ sends $f_q\,dx\,dy$ to area on $B_q$. In particular all halfplane mass fractions through zero are preserved. The two centroids are
$$
g_f=(0,(q-1)/2),\qquad
g_B=\left(\frac8{105\sqrt3},\,\frac{q-1}{2}\frac{232}{135\sqrt3}\right).
$$

For $q=1$ the two coordinate-line sections of $f_q$ and the corresponding chords of $B_q$ are centered at zero, but $g_f=0$ and $g_B\ne0$. For $q=2$ the centroids are nonzero and the direction $(-12,1)$ has strictly positive projection on $g_f$ and strictly negative projection on $g_B$.
title: Exact affine-density Ball transport and centroid reversal
